## Two directions, and why both
The generic path must reproduce every legacy case (none may be lost) AND
must add the cases the dialect could not express (or it has reproduced the
dialect rather than replaced it). A one-directional map would let either
half slip: a shrinking count reads as cleanup, a growing one as progress.
## The 53 are a COUNT here, not a list, and that is a stated gap
Platform's inventory (d7b8ca6a) holds the rows: 33 verifier, 14 builder,
6 type-boundary. They live in Platform's repository and are NOT restated
here -- a copy would be a second authority that drifts. `legacy_total` is
the number this map is accountable to; the Platform lane owns the
row-by-row mapping and must supply it before the parity gate can pass.
## Why the legacy count cannot simply be matched
The dialect collapses provider, binding and verification into ONE
declaration plus an import probe. Shapes it cannot STATE it cannot TEST,
so nine cases below have no legacy counterpart by construction. Passing 53
and adding none of them would mean the generic path reproduced the dialect.
## The ratchet
`legacy_total` and the length of `added` are both fixed. A change in
either direction requires an explicit row change in this file, so a case
cannot appear or vanish as a side effect.
